title: add in the option to install a skill with forced usage
description:
Add --eager flag to prpm install for forced/always-activated skills and agents.

## Final Design (Approved)

### CLI Flag
- `--eager`: Force skill/agent to always activate
- `--lazy`: Revert to default (on-demand) behavior
- Precedence: CLI flag > file-level > package-level > default (lazy)

### prpm.json Schema
```json
{
  "eager": true,  // package-level
  "files": [
    { "path": "file.md", "eager": true }  // file-level override
  ]
}
```

### AGENTS.md Output (Option A)
```markdown
<skills_system priority="0">
<usage>
MANDATORY: You MUST load and apply these skills at the START of every session.
Do not wait for relevance - these are always active.
</usage>
<eager_skills>
<skill activation="eager">...</skill>
</eager_skills>
</skills_system>

<skills_system priority="1">
<!-- existing lazy skills -->
</skills_system>
```

### Applies To
- Skills ✅
- Agents ✅  
- Rules ✅
- Plugins ✅
- Commands ❌ (explicitly invoked)
- Hooks ❌ (trigger-based)

### Fallback Formats
Same eager/lazy pattern applies to: CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, CONVENTIONS.md

add in the ability to make prpm store credentials needed for mcp
description:
Store MCP credentials securely using system keychain (macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, Linux Secret Service).

## Requirements
- Local keychain-based storage (no server dependency)
- Works offline
- Secrets never leave user's machine
- OS handles encryption/secure storage

## Use Case
End users managing MCP credentials centrally - instead of setting env vars everywhere, PRPM manages credentials for MCP packages that need API keys.

## Approach
Use system keychain via library like 'keytar' or native APIs:
- macOS: Keychain
- Windows: Credential Manager  
- Linux: Secret Service (libsecret)

## CLI Interface
Integrated with install flow - when installing MCP package that needs credentials, PRPM prompts user inline.

## Credential Declaration
Package authors can declare required credentials two ways:
1. Explicit `credentials` field in prpm.json: `"credentials": ["GITHUB_TOKEN"]`
2. Inferred from env placeholders in MCP config: `env: { "GITHUB_TOKEN": "${GITHUB_TOKEN}" }`
Explicit declaration takes priority.

## Status
Brainstorming - determining injection mechanism.

description:
The registry and registry-client packages have their own duplicate type definitions (Package, PackageManifest, PackageVersion) instead of importing from the shared @pr-pm/types package. This causes maintenance burden - when adding fields like 'eager', we have to update multiple places.

Scope:
- packages/registry/src/types.ts - Should import/extend from @pr-pm/types
- packages/registry-client/src/registry-client.ts - RegistryPackage should extend/use @pr-pm/types
- packages/registry-client/src/types/registry.ts - Should import from @pr-pm/types

Benefits:
- Single source of truth for type definitions
- Less duplication
- Type changes only need to happen in one place

Risks:
- May need to handle slight differences between DB types and API types
- Could affect downstream consumers

title: Add Amp code editor format support to PRPM
description:
Add support for Amp (https://ampcode.com) AI code editor format.

## Amp Format Overview
Amp supports multiple file types:

### AGENTS.md Files
- Locations: CWD, parent dirs up to $HOME, subtree dirs, ~/.config/amp/AGENTS.md
- Alternatives: AGENT.md, CLAUDE.md (fallback compatibility)
- Format: Plain markdown with optional @-mentions and YAML frontmatter
- Frontmatter: `globs` field for granular guidance (only included when matching files accessed)

### Skills Format
- Directory: `.agents/skills/my-skill/`
- Required: SKILL.md with YAML frontmatter
- Optional: tools/ directory, mcp.json for bundled MCP servers
- Installation locations: .agents/skills/, ~/.config/amp/skills/, .claude/skills/ (compat)
- Frontmatter fields: name (required), description (required), argument-hint, disable-model-invocation

### Custom Commands
- Locations: .agents/commands/, ~/.config/amp/commands/
- Types: Markdown files (.md) or executable files
- Executables: Must have execute bit or shebang, output appended to prompt

### MCP Configuration
- Config key: amp.mcpServers in settings.json
- Supports local and remote servers
- Skill MCP bundling via mcp.json in skill directory

## Implementation Tasks
1. Add 'amp' to Format type in types package
2. Create amp.schema.json, amp-skill.schema.json, amp-command.schema.json
3. Create amp.md format documentation
4. Update canonical.ts with amp format and metadata
5. Create from-amp.ts converter
6. Create to-amp.ts converter
7. Update validation.ts and taxonomy-utils.ts
8. Update CLI filesystem.ts for Amp paths
9. Update CLI format mappings (search.ts, install.ts)
10. Update webapp FORMAT_SUBTYPES and filter dropdown
11. Update registry route schemas
12. Create Amp converter tests

## Reference
- Official docs: https://ampcode.com/manual
- Similar to Claude Code format with differences in frontmatter and directory structure
